title: Morning movement
tomorrow: a poet sits in a ruined city. what does he say is new every morning?

cards: Some mornings the body wakes up stiff and the mind wakes up anxious, and coffee only fixes one of them.

Henry David Thoreau, living in his small cabin by Walden Pond, wrote down what he did with his mornings: "I got up early and bathed in the pond; that was a religious exercise, and one of the best things which I did."
A religious exercise. Not a workout. Why would a swim count as that?

teach.b: Thoreau was one of the Transcendentalists, New England writers who looked for the sacred directly in nature and in the self, not only in churches and creeds.
For him, dawn was holy time. Just before the line about the pond, he says he worshipped Aurora, the dawn, as sincerely as the Greeks did.

teach.h: MORNING IS WHEN I AM AWAKE.
teach.b: A few paragraphs on comes this line: "Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me." So the clock doesn't decide when it's morning. Waking up does.
And for Thoreau, waking up went through the body: the pond, then the woods.
In his essay on walking he says he couldn't keep his health and spirits without sauntering through the woods and fields, free of the world's business. Here is the teaching, named plainly.

The Transcendentalists held that nature is a direct way to the sacred, met with the body and the senses, not only with ideas. The dawn pond was worship because it woke Thoreau to a world he found holy.
That's the difference from a fitness routine, which aims at the body for the body's sake.

teach.h: THROUGH THE BODY, TO BEING AWAKE.
teach.b: Thoreau's swim aimed through the body at being awake.
On your own path, tag still on: move first, not to burn anything, but to arrive. A stretch, a walk around the block, a bow to the light, done the way Thoreau did his pond.

how: Some people on their own paths begin the day the way Thoreau describes: a short stretch, walk or swim, or a bow to the light, as a way of waking up rather than a workout.

o: stretching only so your back doesn't get hurt
a hard workout before breakfast to burn fat
moving your body first, as a way of waking up

p: the dawn he worshipped like the Greeks

s: Thoreau swam every morning mainly for his health
he called it a religious exercise, a way of waking up to a holy world.
for Thoreau, morning is when you wake up, not what the clock says
"Morning is when I am awake and there is a dawn in me."
the Transcendentalists said the sacred is found only in church
they looked for it directly in nature and in the self.

games.q: your friend starts running at dawn. week one it's all pace and calories; week three she says it's the only time she feels awake. which is closer to Thoreau's pond?
o: week three: movement as a way of waking up to the world.
week one: a faster pace makes it a truer practice.
neither; for Thoreau the body didn't matter, only the mind.
games.why: Thoreau's swim aimed through the body at being awake. a holy world was met with the senses, not only with ideas.

practice: Stand and stretch slowly toward the ceiling, then let your arms fall and roll your shoulders back. If there's a window, turn your face toward it, the way Thoreau turned to the dawn, and let whatever light there is reach you.
Let it be your small version of Thoreau's pond: a way of waking up, not a workout.

wordCard.voice: Morning movement: moving first, to wake up rather than to work out. For Thoreau, a dawn swim was a religious exercise.

carryVoice: Keep this one: move first, and let the body wake the rest of you. See you in the morning.
